name: Mineta San Jose International Airport
before:
The Bay Area's second busiest airport after San Francisco, and by some distance the most convenient. It is three miles north west of downtown San Jose, against roughly fourteen miles for San Francisco and ten for Oakland, so for a client working in Santa Clara County this is the one to price first.

Southwest dominates. In 2021 it carried 54 per cent of everyone using the airport, with Alaska Airlines second on about 19 per cent. The airport is also a United States customs port of entry.

Traffic peaked at 15.7 million passengers in 2019, having passed its old 2001 record in 2018.

The closeness to town cuts both ways. The airport is hemmed in by the city with very little room to expand, and its approach paths cap how tall buildings in downtown San Jose are allowed to be under FAA rules.

There are two parallel runways, each 11,000 feet, on a 1,050 acre site. It is named after Norman Mineta, a San Jose native who was the city's mayor and later United States Secretary of Transportation and of Commerce.
after:
The Bay Area's second busiest airport after San Francisco, a few miles north west of downtown San Jose. For a client working in Santa Clara County it is the most convenient of the region's three main airports and the one to price first.

Southwest dominates, carrying more than half of all passengers. The airport is also a United States customs port of entry.

It handled about 10.7 million passengers in 2025, almost 10 per cent fewer than in 2024 and still well short of its 2019 peak of more than 15.5 million.

The closeness to town cuts both ways: the airport's flight paths limit how tall buildings in downtown San Jose can be.

There are two parallel runways, each 11,000 feet long. It is named after Norman Mineta, a San Jose native who was the city's mayor and later United States Secretary of Commerce and of Transportation.

claims.claim: a few miles from downtown San Jose
claims.inAfter: a few miles north west of downtown San Jose
claims.note: Was 'three miles'. The sources do not agree on a figure: the FAA's master record gives 2 nautical miles (2.3 statute miles) from the central business district; the coordinates give 2.5 miles in a straight line; the operator says 3 miles on its About page but 'Four miles north of downtown' in its own 2025 financial report; Wikipedia says 3 miles in one place and 'less than 4 miles' in another. As the brief directs, the figure is dropped and the direction kept. Every source puts it between two and four miles, which is 'a few'.

Two current measures, both over half: the operator's own table gives Southwest 54.1 per cent of enplanements in fiscal 2025 (July 2024 to June 2025), and BTS gives it 61.61 per cent of passengers on US flights in the twelve months to June 2026. The operator's table also confirms the 2021 figure (54.2 per cent in fiscal 2021).

claims.note: New, replacing the 2019 peak as the answer to how busy it is now. This is TOTAL passengers, arrivals plus departures: the operator's calendar-year 2025 report gives 10,675,167 (5,327,346 enplaned, 5,347,821 deplaned). The FAA's preliminary CY2025 table counts 5,257,421 revenue enplanements (boardings only, about half of total passengers), consistent with the operator's figure. Same pairing as the PIT and CHS ledgers.

claims.claim: fourteen miles for San Francisco and ten for Oakland
claims.wasBefore: against roughly fourteen miles for San Francisco and ten for Oakland
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. It also measures each of the other airports from its own downtown, which says nothing about the drive from Santa Clara County.

claims.claim: Southwest 54 per cent in 2021
claims.wasBefore: In 2021 it carried 54 per cent of everyone using the airport
claims.why: Five years old. Replaced by the current share, more than half on both the operator's fiscal 2025 table and BTS's twelve months to June 2026.

claims.claim: Alaska Airlines second on about 19 per cent
claims.wasBefore: with Alaska Airlines second on about 19 per cent
claims.why: Out of date. Alaska's share has fallen from 18.6 per cent of enplanements in fiscal 2021 to 13.3 per cent in fiscal 2025 (operator, including its SkyWest and Horizon flights), and BTS puts Alaska-operated flights at 8.02 per cent in the twelve months to June 2026, behind SkyWest (8.68 per cent), which flies for several airlines. Whether Alaska is still second depends on how that regional flying is counted, so no rank is given.

claims.wasBefore: Traffic peaked at 15.7 million passengers in 2019
claims.why: The two sources give 15.6 and 15.7 million; the text now says more than 15.5 million, which both support, next to the 2025 figure.

claims.claim: passed its 2001 record in 2018
claims.wasBefore: having passed its old 2001 record in 2018
claims.why: Wikipedia alone (14.3 million in 2018 against 14.2 million in 2001). The operator's archive of activity reports online starts in 2023.

claims.claim: hemmed in with very little room to expand
claims.wasBefore: The airport is hemmed in by the city with very little room to expand
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. San José Spotlight (April 2024) describes expansion plans as paused, not blocked, and quotes the council's airport liaison: 'There is a long term plan for the airport to expand'.

claims.claim: under FAA rules

claims.why: The second source speaks of flight safety requirements and height restrictions near the airport without naming the FAA in its own text; the limit itself is kept.

claims.claim: 1,050 acre site
claims.why: Sources disagree: the FAA master record and Wikipedia say 1,050 acres, the operator's 2025 financial report 1,124 acres.

opinion.text: it is the most convenient of the region's three main airports and the one to price first
opinion.why: The old text's advice, kept: the airport is in San Jose and serves Santa Clara County (Wikipedia, the operator, the FAA), where San Francisco and Oakland are further up the bay.

opinion.text: The closeness to town cuts both ways
opinion.why: The old text's lead-in; the height limit it introduces is sourced.
